newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka opposition urges members to give up guns.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka opposition urges members to give up guns.

text.p: Sri Lanka's main opposition United National Party (UNP) on Friday said it had urged party activists to avoid violence and heed a government call to hand in unlicenced firearms in the run-up to this month's election.

"We have passed down instructions to all our members not to get involved in violence and focus on just the election," opposition leader and former prime minister Ranil Wickremesinghe told a news conference.
The election for local bodies, the first popularity test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's ruling People's Alliance coalition government, is scheduled for March 21.

Politicians and political activists in Sri Lanka own a large number of guns, many unlicenced, to protect themselves against possible attack by Tamil rebels who are fighting a separatist war in the island's north and east.
An independent group on Friday said that 770 acts of violence, including four killings and 176 cases of assault, had been reported since February 5 when nominations for the election closed.

Supporters of the ruling alliance were alleged to have been responsible for 253 of the reported incidents, while UNP supporters were allegedly responsible for 129, the Centre for Monitoring Election Violence said in a statement.

The election already has been marred by the killing of a young ruling coalition legislator last month, which was followed by two days of riots in the legislator's constituency of Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) southeast of the capital Colombo.
A UNP member of parliament and a former UNP mayor are among the suspects detained by police for the killing.
After the killing, the government launched a crackdown on illegal weapons used by politicians and granted an amnesty untill March 15 for the surrender of weapons.
On Thursday, Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte told parliament that revolvers, shotguns and machine guns were among the 1,419 unlicenced firearms recovered by police
Some 1,878 unlicenced firearms were still held by politicians and their supporters, Ratwatte said.
